goals: Choose the right chart for a question
Use histograms, box plots and scatter plots for EDA
Spot outliers, skew and relationships visually
why: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) catches data errors, outliers and leakage before they ruin a model. Anscombe's quartet shows four datasets with identical statistics but completely different pictures.
explain: **Histogram**: the shape of one numeric variable. Is it symmetric, skewed, or does it have two peaks?
**Box plot**: median, quartiles and outliers. Great for comparing a number across groups (salary by department).
**Scatter plot**: the relationship between two numbers. Look for trends, curves, clusters and outliers.
**Bar chart** for counts per category; **line chart** for values over time. Always label axes with units.

example.title: A box plot by hand: delivery times
steps: Median = (30 + 31) / 2 = 30.5; Q1 = 27.25, Q3 = 34.5 (NumPy's default), so IQR = 7.25
75 lies above 45.375 → drawn as an outlier dot; every other value is inside the fences
Mean = 344 / 10 = 34.4, almost 4 minutes above the median because of that one order
example.result: Typical delivery ≈ 30 minutes, plus one 75-minute case to investigate. The box plot shows both at a glance; the mean alone blends them into a misleading 34.4. A scatter of time vs distance would then tell you whether 75 was simply a long trip or a real problem.

mistakes: Computing statistics without ever looking at the data.
Pie charts with many slices; truncated y-axes on bar charts.
takeaways: Histogram = distribution, box = groups and outliers, scatter = relationships

practice.code:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
t = pd.Series([22, 25, 27, 28, 30, 31, 33, 35, 38, 75], name="minutes")
q1, q3 = np.percentile(t, [25, 75]); iqr = q3 - q1
print(t.median(), q1, q3, q3 + 1.5 * iqr, t.mean())  # 30.5 27.25 34.5 45.375 34.4
t.plot.box(); plt.show()          # 75 appears as an outlier dot
t.plot.hist(bins=6); plt.show()   # shape of the distribution
practice.note: Charts need a plotting backend, so run this in Jupyter or VS Code rather than in the in-browser runner.

check.why: Box plots compare medians, spread and outliers side by side.
